title: Prove marking sessions done, stopping, deleting and reopening in Node Vitest

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage

**Verdict: Caught.** The maintained deletion proof caught the missing guard for both a listed working session and an unlisted session marked Done.

**Story and revision.** `SEED-413#prove-native-session-and-terminal-lifecycle-on-vitest` at `b809bfb23f683a3a6aed510a0f5411451a242fe3`. The selected promise is that a known session keeps its recorded entry and the deletion answer carries its state. Plan 867 slice 7 and `dashboard/backend-tests/sessions/agent-launch-delete.spec.ts` own this promise.

**Fault and observation.** In an isolated detached checkout, I made the early `state-known` return in `dashboard/server/launchRecordDeletion.ts` unreachable by adding `&& false` to `!recordDeletable(joined)`. The native-state read, fixtures and assertions were unchanged. The two observed inputs use a private kept-record store and the existing fake Claude listing. A separate scratch invocation observed the working native session as available, loaded and working, and the unlisted Done session as unavailable with its Done timestamp. For each input a fresh store read found the record before the faulted request. The answer was `deleted` and another store read found the record gone.

**Maintained evidence.** The same `npm run test:dashboard:backend -- 'sessions/agent-launch-delete\.spec\.ts$' --workers=1` command ran on the clean, faulted and restored revisions with Node Vitest. All six cases passed on the clean baseline. With the fault, only the two cases that keep the working or unlisted Done session failed. Both failed at `agent-launch-delete.spec.ts:154`, where the maintained assertion expected a `state-known` answer carrying the target session's state and received `deleted`. The separate witness establishes the lost record because that early assertion stops each case before its later kept-record assertion. After restoration, all six cases passed again. The scratch checkout matched its original HEAD and clean status and was then removed. The exact runs, exit receipts, fault diff and witness are in `/tmp/dough-867-intent.TITKR8dU`.

The narrower title filter found the unexpanded `test.each` template in the selector, then its proof adapter reported no result for the template. The file-level command was the smallest maintained selection that reached both concrete cases. This probe assessed those two known-state paths.

**Next proof action.** Retain the existing known-state cases. The observed fault requires no stronger proof or follow-up. No already-planned repair applies to this probe.

- **Test runtime.** 5,691 ms measured inside the backend runner across the comparable baseline, faulted and restored runs, respectively 1,779 ms, 1,963 ms and 1,949 ms. The unsuccessful preliminary title selection used a further 3,190 ms in the runner.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable. The invocation provides no independent human-effort measurement.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable. No separate active-time or token measurement was attributable to this probe.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 123798 ms (measured), from 1795741590689 to 1795741714487 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.


## Wrap-up disposition

Checked `b809bfb23f683a3a6aed510a0f5411451a242fe3`. Caught on both known-state paths. No follow-up is needed for the observed fault.
